summary: Seeded AI context layer from current repository state and prior project memory. Current main includes continuous biology, PDE/IC/BC loss assembly, Wang-style gradient-statistic weighting, causal time curriculum, final-bias IC initialisation, and fixed-grid diagnostics.
next_action: Append future training/validation runs here with command, config, key metrics, interpretation, and next action.

summary: All-feature Causal R3 run avoided near-zero collapse but produced nearly time-invariant outputs. Scalar loss decreased strongly, but fixed-grid PDE diagnostics improved only early then worsened: fixed_pde bottomed around step 450 and res_p95 around step 500 before rising by step 2000. Timestep loss was effectively inactive because lambda_timestep=1e-4 and Wang weighting reduced w_timestep to ~7.9e-3, making the final timestep contribution ~7.7e-7. IC weight also fell to ~2e-3. BC flux was clamped for 100% of boundary evaluations throughout, so BC diagnostics remain numerically suspect.
interpretation: Most likely causes are gated PDE loss from --causal-r3-weight-pde-loss, weak timestep anchoring, fixed R3 time slabs with only x resampling, and Wang downweighting of IC/timestep anchors. Training longer alone is unlikely to fix this unless temporal constraints are made meaningful.
next_action: Run ablation removing --causal-r3-weight-pde-loss while keeping Causal R3 scoring; increase lambda_timestep to 1e-2 and timestep_n_pairs to 8; compare output temporal variance and fixed-grid diagnostics.

summary: Reviewed six 40k-step single-species PINN runs using log PDE residual, relative recruitment-boundary loss, constant recruitment R=3711296885, lambda_pde=lambda_ic=lambda_bc=1, CPU training, and R3/Causal-R3 variants. The strongest empirical result is the simple plain-R3 setup with lr=3e-4, n_time=10, n_eval=30, r3_population_size=300, r3_update_every=5, r3_warmup_steps=100, r3_score_form=abs, seed=123. User judged this run very good by eye, matching the R/mizer reference as closely as visual inspection can assess. More complex causal/timestep/weighting variants mostly failed by becoming time-invariant, loss-dominated by IC or timestep terms, or showing boundary artefacts near the smallest weight after the initial condition.

runs.label: plain_r3_lr3e4_pop300_best_visual_match
runs.user_result: Very very good; visually as close to R/mizer output as eye test can assess.
runs.interpretation: Current empirical baseline. Preserve as reference before adding extra mechanisms. Note this command did not explicitly pass --disable-wang-weights, so confirm from config/history whether Wang weights were active or inert in this exact run before attributing success to disabled weighting.

runs.label: causal_r3_lr3e5_timestep0p3_wang_bad
runs.command_core: --n-steps 40000 --n-time 10 --n-eval 30 --lr 3e-5 --residual-form log --boundary-loss-form relative --bc-use-constant-r --bc-constant-r 3711296885 --lambda-pde 1 --lambda-ic 1 --lambda-bc 1 --lambda-timestep 0.3 --collocation-strategy causal-r3 --r3-population-size 300 --r3-update-every 5 --r3-warmup-steps 100 --r3-score-form abs --r3-seed 123 --weight-update-every 10 --weight-warmup-steps 100 --weight-alpha 0.05 --weight-min 1e-3 --weight-max 1e3 --causal-curriculum linear --causal-start-fraction 0.05 --causal-ramp-steps 5000 --causal-r3-alpha 5 --causal-r3-gamma-init -0.5 --causal-r3-gamma-max 1.5 --device cpu
runs.user_result: Not good. Almost no change across time. Correct-ish scale but incorrect dynamics. Loss dominated by timestep loss.
runs.interpretation: lambda_timestep=0.3 is too large for this setup, especially with low lr and adaptive weighting. Do not use large timestep loss until its scale is calibrated against PDE/IC/BC objective contributions.

runs.label: causal_r3_lr3e5_timestep0_wang_better_shape_time_invariant
runs.command_core: --n-steps 40000 --n-time 10 --n-eval 30 --lr 3e-5 --residual-form log --boundary-loss-form relative --bc-use-constant-r --bc-constant-r 3711296885 --lambda-pde 1 --lambda-ic 1 --lambda-bc 1 --lambda-timestep 0 --collocation-strategy causal-r3 --r3-population-size 300 --r3-update-every 5 --r3-warmup-steps 100 --r3-score-form abs --r3-seed 123 --weight-update-every 10 --weight-warmup-steps 100 --weight-alpha 0.05 --weight-min 1e-3 --weight-max 1e3 --causal-curriculum linear --causal-start-fraction 0.05 --causal-ramp-steps 5000 --causal-r3-alpha 5 --causal-r3-gamma-init -0.5 --causal-r3-gamma-max 1.5 --device cpu
runs.user_result: Better shape than timestep=0.3, but still little/no change through time. Loss stops having useful effect after ~15000 iterations and fluctuates by about two orders of magnitude. Initial condition dominates loss.
runs.interpretation: Removing timestep domination improves profile shape but not temporal dynamics. Causal curriculum plus low lr plus Wang weighting is still suspect. IC domination suggests loss balance/constraint geometry is not producing the required temporal evolution.

runs.label: causal_r3_gated_lr3e4_pop600_disable_wang_time_invariant
runs.command_core: --n-steps 40000 --n-time 20 --n-eval 30 --lr 3e-4 --residual-form log --boundary-loss-form relative --bc-use-constant-r --bc-constant-r 3711296885 --lambda-pde 1 --lambda-ic 1 --lambda-bc 1 --lambda-timestep 0 --collocation-strategy causal-r3 --r3-population-size 600 --r3-update-every 5 --r3-warmup-steps 100 --r3-score-form abs --r3-seed 123 --disable-wang-weights --causal-curriculum off --causal-r3-weight-pde-loss --causal-r3-alpha 5 --causal-r3-gamma-init -0.5 --causal-r3-gamma-max 1.5 --device cpu
runs.user_result: Correct shape but no change over time. After the initial condition there is a large jump at smallest w, suggesting boundary-condition artefact. Loss mainly initial condition and does not seem to decrease; each loss term fluctuates strongly iteration-to-iteration.
runs.interpretation: True causal PDE gating does not solve time invariance and may suppress useful later-time PDE pressure. Boundary artefact at w_min means the recruitment-boundary implementation/weighting needs diagnostic review before more training hyperparameter search.

runs.label: plain_r3_lr3e4_pop600_disable_wang_same_as_prior
runs.user_result: Same as prior output. Does not improve time dynamics over the previous problematic result.
runs.interpretation: Simply increasing n_time/population from 300 to 600 is not enough. The failure is probably not just sparse collocation coverage.

runs.label: plain_r3_lr3e4_n30_eval60_pop600_disable_wang_same_as_prior
runs.interpretation: More nominal time/eval arguments do not help when r3_population_size remains 600; effective R3 points are still population-size constrained. Do not expect further improvement from just raising n_time/n_eval unless the effective population and diagnostics justify it.

cross_run_interpretation: The current best empirical path is the simple plain-R3 baseline at lr=3e-4 and population 300. Failed variants show that causal-R3, causal PDE gating, high timestep weight, and larger R3 populations do not automatically recover temporal dynamics. Repeated time-invariant outputs plus w_min jump point away from generic optimiser tuning and toward constraint formulation: boundary condition behaviour at the recruitment edge, timestep-loss scaling, and whether the PDE/IC/BC combination actually imposes the observed temporal trajectory.
next_action: Use the best plain-R3 run as the reference baseline. Before proposing more large training runs, inspect saved config/history/fixed diagnostics for the best and failed runs: objective_loss_pde/ic/bc/timestep, w_pde/w_ic/w_bc/w_timestep, bc_valid_fraction, bc_target_N ranges, boundary_residual_abs_p95/max, fixed residual fields, and temporal variance of output_diagnostics. Next modelling tests should be small ablations: (1) reduce lambda_ic after warm start or add scheduled IC weight, (2) run with lambda_bc=0 to isolate whether the w_min jump is BC-driven, (3) test weak timestep loss only after calibrating its objective scale, e.g. lambda_timestep far below 0.3, and (4) avoid causal PDE gating until plain-R3 diagnostics are understood.
